The request does not fabricate contents or collect them. Back outside after success, credit the promised 300 c once to each actually owned hero; party treasure markers and per-hero reward markers are distinct. No generic quest completion/abandonment, dead/missing hero entitlement, XP or additional loot amount is inferred. Step loot: As the final demon is slayed, heroes loot 2 objective chests (unlocked, not trapped, just roll on the Treasure Tables). Step treasure_handoff: Request two actual unlocked/untrapped objective-chest outcomes once without inventing contents. Step hero_reward: Once back in the fresh air again, the wizard and Jarl give the promised reward (300 c per hero).
- `procedure.closing_portal_demon_group`: Structural reading, not printed text: For one separately owned actual initial group (first or second) or actual encounter result multiple of 10, persist a single demon-type d6 selection and resolve its printed group quantity once. Initial groups and replacement groups use d6 quantities for types 1–4 and d3 for 5/6. Later spawning uses one demon and cannot enter this group procedure. Missing quantity retains the selected type; replay cannot change species, quantity or duplicate actors. Demon statistics/Cursed Weapons and actual placement/battle remain dependencies. Step initial_context: Authorize one of the two actual initial groups. Step replacement_context: All encounter results of even 10s (10, 20, 30...) result in an encounter with random demons. Step request_group: Request unresolved actual dice once; table lookup is not a generated group. Step snapshot_type: Persist selected actual type before delayed quantity resolution. Step actual_quantity: Copy actual supplied result to owned working state without changing supplied inputs. Step group_1: Resolve only the selected type and its actual quantity within the printed dice bounds once. Step group_2: Resolve only the selected type and its actual quantity within the printed dice bounds once. Step group_3: Resolve only the selected type and its actual quantity within the printed dice bounds once.
- `procedure.closing_portal_preparation`: Structural reading, not printed text: Initialize Silver City, eight corridors/eight rooms, supplied ritual scroll and advertised 300 c once. Actual initial d6 initializes current/start/minimum Threat once, maximum 20. Actual objective entry records portal/hero geometry and requests exactly two independently owned initial groups and actual random placement once; a request does not resolve quantities, place actors or execute battle. Step setup: The wizard provides the team with a scroll which could be cast by one with very limited skills in the Arcane Arts. Quest Location: In Silver City. Number of Tiles: 8 corridors, 8 rooms. Reward: 300 c per hero. Step request_threat: Request the actual initial d6 once without inferring it from current Threat. Step initial_threat: Initial d6, minimum same as start, maximum 20; preserve later current Threat on replay. Step objective_setup: In the centre of the room over a large summoning circle is a shimmering bubble. Roll twice on the special rules Encounter Table and place demons randomly in the room. Heroes enter centred along the long side. Step first_group: Hand off this actual objective-room preparation once; requests do not resolve dice or placement. Step second_group: Hand off this actual objective-room preparation once; requests do not resolve dice or placement. Step placement: Hand off this actual objective-room preparation once; requests do not resolve dice or placement.
- `procedure.closing_portal_reading_attempt`: Structural reading, not printed text: Initial actual eligible stationary objective-room reading lasts 1d6+1. Persist duration once. Any interruption or movement resets progress and requires starting over. Restart only on an actual new start-over event with supplied unresolved duration context. Count each actual complete chronological reading turn once, inspect its interruptions before progress, and seal the portal at the required uninterrupted duration. Closure stops reading and still requires all demons to be killed. No first spawn phase, within-turn spawn ordering, universal restart dice policy, chest collection or reward is invented. Step missing_duration: An actual first-attempt d6 is required; no duration or restart policy is inferred. Step start: Reading can be done from anywhere in the room. Roll 1d6+1 for duration. They must hold still while reading it. Step consume_interrupted_turn: An actually completed interrupted reading turn cannot be counted again after start-over; preserve its supplied chronological identity without granting reading progress. Step interruption: If the character is interrupted in any way (wounded, dodges, or parries), they have to start over. They must hold still while reading. Step unresolved_restart: Start-over duration policy is absent; pending context cannot resume reading or choose a roll. Step restart: Actual source start-over resets progress only after duration context is supplied, without choosing a universal dice policy. Step unresolved_turn_context: The source does not define within-turn boundaries; unresolved actual context cannot advance or close reading. Step reading_turn: Count one actually completed uninterrupted stationary turn once, after interruption checks. Preserve chronological consumption across restarts. Step closure: Seal only at the actual completed uninterrupted reading duration; all remaining demons still must be killed.
- `procedure.closing_portal_single_spawn`: Structural reading, not printed text: Every other turn one demon emerges while the portal is open. Require actual supplied schedule and chronological event ordering; no first phase/modulo convention or same-turn closure priority is invented. Consume an actual new spawn event once, then resolve its type d6 only. Group quantities never apply. A type handoff is not a roll; a pending already-emerged demon may receive its type after closure without spawning another. Never overwrite a pending earlier event with a later spawn. Statistics, placement and battle are separately owned. Step unresolved_schedule: Unresolved schedule/within-turn ordering cannot create a spawn. Step request_type: Request the missing type once for this already-emerged single demon. Step actual_type: Resolve supplied type-only d6 to owned state, without reading group quantity. Step type_1: Apply selected source type/equipment/Armour 0 only; one demon remains one. Step type_2: Apply selected source type/equipment/Armour 0 only; one demon remains one. Step type_3: Apply selected source type/equipment/Armour 0 only; one demon remains one.
- `procedure.combat_aim`: Overwatch with Ranged Weapons (PDF 107, printed 105) says "Perks and Talents may be used during this shot, but not for aiming." That limits Perks and Talents used for aiming during an Overwatch shot; it does not forbid the Aim action, so this procedure has no Overwatch condition.
- `procedure.combat_turn`: The chart asks "Last token in the bag?" only on the branch where the drawn token has no unacted Hero/Mercenary or Enemy left; every "Perform" box loops straight back to "Pull initiative token". It does not show what happens when the model of the last token in the bag has acted.
- `procedure.damage_follow_up`: Magic Damage: some creatures like demons suffer further complications. The passage gives no creature-specific definitions or numeric effects; retain supplied source-backed applicability/outcomes, without inventing Bestiary contents or a universal demon vulnerability.
- `procedure.dead_rising_campaign`: Each campaign quest runs as its own accepted quest and dungeon lifecycle (procedure.quest_acceptance); this procedure holds only the campaign order, the Silver City start of the second quest, the 6A/6B choice and the once-only Campaign aftermath.
- `procedure.dead_rising_campaign`: Quest 2: The Dead Rising prints no onward destination in its aftermath; the next destination recorded is the printed Quest Location of Quest 3: Highwaymen, White 34.
- `procedure.dead_rising_campaign`: The Burning Village continues the campaign whether the heroes won or fled: both aftermath branches print onward travel (to the city / to Silver city).
- `procedure.dead_rising_campaign`: league_member records the enlistment that High King Logan III has requested the Jarl to make in the Campaign aftermath.
- `procedure.dead_rising_campaign`: The campaign text does not say what happens to the campaign when one of its quests is failed or abandoned (issue.quest.campaign_progression_boundaries); such an outcome does not advance the campaign here.
- `procedure.dead_rising_campaign`: Campaign and step ownership checks bind one campaign instance; they encode no printed sentence beyond the campaign start rule.
- `procedure.dungeon_generation`: Exploration Card contents and shuffled orders are supplied outcomes. Abandoning your Quest and Finishing your Quest are modelled by state_machine.quest_dungeon and procedure.quest_dungeon_lifecycle.
- `procedure.dungeon_route`: Stack orders are supplied outcomes; no card inventory, shuffle algorithm or geometric layout is invented.
- `procedure.encounters`: The encounter-free streak count, the room-description modifier and the Bestiary table outcome are caller-supplied; the Bestiary is not present, so no enemy selection is invented.
- `procedure.enemy_attack`: Target may: the defence options, thresholds and use limits are procedure.hero_defence; this procedure takes its supplied result.
- `procedure.enemy_attack`: DMG- Shield’s DEF transferred to arm and arm armour: the chart draws this box into the line that reaches "Roll 1d6 for hit area"; Parry with a Shield (PDF 120) sends the rest of the damage to the arm. This procedure hands the spillover to procedure.combat_damage and does not roll a hit area for it.
- `procedure.estate_furnishing`: Training Grounds and Archery Range may each be used once between each visit to a dungeon, and each hero trains at one or the other; a hero who trained at the other facility is refused in the same interval, and whether the choice is permanent is not stated. The Alchemist Lab allows one recipe and the Garden one gathering; whether that limit is per facility or per alchemist is not stated, so the caller supplies the reading. The Wizard’s Study (for a wizard) and the Kennel state no use limit. The text does not say how often the Smithy, Shrine or Crops can be used.
- `procedure.estate_ghostly_events`: Hero effects for the coming quest are handed to their owners; this procedure owns the once-per-interval roll, the event chosen and the estate state it changes. The book does not say whether the roll needs a night at the estate, whether an owed Ghostly Event 8 replaces the rolls, or where crop rations are held; the caller supplies each reading, and the procedure waits on an issue until it does.
- `procedure.estate_ghostly_events`: The roll is printed under Staying at the House. Whether it applies when the party did not spend that night at the estate is the ghost_roll_scope reading. After a failed Grieving Mother, an owed event #8 is the interval’s event under the replaces_rolls reading; under the in_addition reading it applies once and the ordinary contact roll is also made. Each new interval is decided afresh on every call.
- `procedure.estate_ownership`: Staying at the House prints storage but no retrieval rule; the retrieve step only lets the owning party take back the item it stored, so that storage is not one-way.
- `procedure.first_blood`: Monster card and monster equipment card values are not printed here; card outcomes are supplied and no statistics are invented.
- `procedure.first_blood`: Each of the four adversaries gets its own randomised board edge and 1d10 distance, persisted once.
- `procedure.first_blood`: The +2 initiative tokens apply to the first turn only and are handed to procedure.initiative once; later turns report no bonus.
- `procedure.first_blood`: The aftermath requests settlement arrival once; the actual arrival and settlement event completion are separate. No coins, XP or treasure are printed for this quest.
- `procedure.guild_access`: The book prints no guild membership fee, enrolment sequence or membership rank; access_granted is therefore per operation, not persistent membership.
- `procedure.guild_item_service`: The book prints the service fees but not how payment, Activity Points or lodging are accounted. The procedure charges the fee once per authorized operation and item, requires the fee to be affordable, and leaves activity time and lodging to settlement accounting.
- `procedure.guild_item_service`: Staves whose catalogue rows print a different recharge outcome (for example the Arcane Staff and Staff of the Heart) keep that outcome; the charge reset applies the printed three-charge default.
- `procedure.guild_item_service`: PDF 153 and 158 print no Activity Point cost or duration for recharging or blessing, so activity_authorized and duration_completed follow the settlement activity rules (Guilds, PDF 145; Activities in a Settlement and Leaving on a Quest, PDF 133).
- `procedure.guild_purchase_authorization`: The guild pages print what each guild sells, its price and its availability but no separate purchase sequence. This procedure only authorizes the purchase (access, completed activity and a resolved catalogue offering) and hands the quote to ordinary settlement purchasing, which makes the Availability Roll, charges the price and changes inventory exactly once.
- `procedure.guild_skill_training`: Skill Training costs 1 Activity Point in the Available Actions table; only the Inner Sanctum also states "takes 1 day".
- `procedure.guild_skill_training`: The natural skill maximum of 80 applies to trained skills. The book prints no partial +1 or +2 session or prorated fee when a full +3 would exceed 80 (issue.guild.training_near_cap).
- `procedure.hate_talent`: Step report: marks the check unresolved until the owned check context is established.
- `procedure.hate_talent`: Step clear_inactive: with no owned Talent, no confirmed check or a phase other than attack, parry or dodge, only this contribution is cleared.
- `procedure.hate_talent`: Step request_context: a missing enemy match or unresolved check scope is requested once without asserting a zero contribution.
- `procedure.hate_talent`: Step reset_known: the fixed contribution is recomputed for each resolved check; replays do not accumulate.
- `procedure.hero_defence`: Fast (PDF 179) lets a weapon parry once per turn outside Parry Stance and damages the weapon on 90-00. The procedure applies the 90-00 damage to that out-of-stance Fast parry only; a Fast weapon parrying in Parry Stance uses the 95-00 Parry with a Weapon rule (issue.combat.fast_parry_in_stance).
- `procedure.hero_spell_casting`: Execute effect of spell: the effect itself is the spell record (Appendix IV), not this procedure.
- `procedure.hero_spell_casting`: Make skill check (CS+20) for Touch spells: the touch test is core.magic.touch; its parry and dodge resolution belongs to Combat.
- `procedure.hero_spell_casting`: Enemy spell caster present and able to dispel?: the chart asks this only on the Ranged? branch. The Touch? branch runs AA → CS+20 → Execute effect of spell and the Incantation? branch runs Success? → Execute effect of spell, so neither reaches the box, and Dispelling Magic prints "Touch spells or Close Combat Spells cannot be dispelled."
- `procedure.humanoid_close_combat_behaviour`: Check the Bestiary to see if the enemy has any such abilities: whether the enemy has a Skill or Special Talent is supplied as has_skill_or_talent; the Bestiary is not present.
- `procedure.humanoid_close_combat_behaviour`: One run of this procedure chooses one action. Starting over from the top once the action is performed is combat.enemy_behaviour.top_down.
- `procedure.initiative`: Counts are caller-supplied eligible models. Spell/rest/quest bonus-token outcomes are explicit inputs, not inferred actions.
- `procedure.irrational_fear`: Randomise between the five printed factions: the selection method/weights are not specified.
- `procedure.irrational_fear`: Fear: actual reaction timing/eligibility/resolution is supplied separately; no canonical resolver id is invented.
- `procedure.locked_door_and_close`: AP totals are recorded as source requirements; per-turn retry sequencing requires caller-supplied state.
- `procedure.lost_brother_personal_quest`: Steps run in printed order; each step executes its cited rules, whose own conditions select the branch (dead at 60 or higher, alive below 60, later death reverting to the dead result). The page prints no order between the burial and the rescue branches beyond the branch conditions.
- `procedure.open_portcullis`: Each paid 1 AP attempt is paired with its own supplied STR Test result and helper count; a missing or mismatched result leaves that attempt pending rather than resolving another one.
- `procedure.poison_cure`: Chapel of Metheia back in the city (PDF122): no dedicated Chapel service/location ID is bound. Do not equate Chapel with Temple or inherit Sick Ward treatment accounting.
- `procedure.quest_acceptance`: Structural reading, not printed text: offer rolls, the Luck prohibition and the rejection limits belong to procedure.settlement_arrival. This checkpoint records one accepted choice per party and distinct quest occurrence, with separate main and side records and an immutable originating settlement and site. Request steps hand off to the supplied quest choice or site roll once; the handoff is not acceptance. Departure, progression, abandonment, completion and rewards belong to their own procedures, and a fresh record does not reset an earlier occurrence.
- `procedure.quest_departure`: Structural reading, not printed text: procedure.settlement_activities_and_overnight owns occupied days, lodging, departure eligibility and the no-activity departure day. This checkpoint requests that departure once, then records only a result for the same party, accepted occurrence and day. Departure is not arrival at the Quest Site, progress, completion, payment or a reset of hero recovery or attempts.
- `procedure.quest_dungeon_lifecycle`: Structural reading, not printed text: this procedure composes the existing accepted occurrence and actual initial departure with actual dungeon entry. Abandonment records the actual layout, retaining acceptance, quest provenance, tasks and rewards. A distinct actual return visit resumes the same occurrence and requests source repopulation and fresh door and encounter checks. Confirmed repopulation is a supplied outcome; invocation alone changes no actors. Source task achievement permits exit without retracing; permission is not actual exit. Repeat eligibility creates a distinct accepted occurrence through existing acceptance and never resets this one. Source-specific progress and rewards stay owned by their procedures. This unit is dungeon-only, not a universal personal or wilderness quest policy.
- `procedure.quest_reading_and_events`: Reading permission follows the actual quest occurrence: reaching the Quest Room permits text to the second border, completing the quest permits the aftermath.
- `procedure.quest_reading_and_events`: An aftermath finding is handed off once and is distinct from tile-drawn treasure; its collection and any resource accounting are supplied by the caller, not credited here.
- `procedure.quest_reading_and_events`: Each actual Threat change is consumed once in chronological order; falling below XX and increasing back to XX triggers again, as the printed example shows.
- `procedure.quest_reading_and_events`: General individual repeatability is handed to acceptance eligibility for a distinct quest occurrence (procedure.quest_acceptance).
- `procedure.random_quest_selection`: One selection belongs to one random quest offer; a later offer, including a repeat of the same quest, starts a fresh selection.
- `procedure.random_quest_selection`: A result of 6 (Roll Again) rolls the table again; the first 1–5 result selects the Objective Room and is kept for the offer.
- `procedure.random_quest_selection`: The page prints no die or result mapping for the second-stage chapter quest roll, so the chapter quest is a supplied outcome (issue.quest.random_quest_second_stage).
- `procedure.random_quest_selection`: Acceptance, departure and the quest itself are separate procedures; the handoff does not accept or start the quest.
- `procedure.ranger_special_talent`: The book does not say where the tutor fee is paid or whether "at any time" needs a settlement visit. Requiring Silver City, Rangers’ Guild access and an authorized, completed settlement activity is a reading the page does not print (issue.guild.ranger_talent_any_time).
- `procedure.returning_relic`: Structural reading, not printed text: Initialize Random location, 8+8 tiles and actual d4+1 Threat once (minimum=start, maximum 20). Preserve quest-owned Luck nullification until actual stone return without changing numeric Luck Points. Source Scenario trigger 8–10 requests Threat resolution for each distinct actual die event. Actual objective entry records geometry and requests two independent Encounter Table outcomes/random placement. An actual owned once-per-turn refit after all enemies are dead and in front of the statue requires a DEX test. Persist pending attempt and actual result ownership. Success returns stone and ends only this nullification; failure records +1 Threat and applies it once below 20, with maximum-boundary accounting unresolved. Home arrival after return pays each actual owned hero 300 c once. No generic completion, abandoned-quest effect, new Luck amount, XP, objective chest or automatic journey is invented. Step nullification: Maintain only this quest-owned nullification; numeric Luck and other curses are independently owned. Step setup: Return a polished black stone to its statue in a forgotten temple. Random location, eight corridors, eight rooms, 300 c per hero. Step request_threat: Request actual initial d4 once. Step initial_threat: Printed start 1d4+1, minimum same as start and maximum 20; never reseed later Threat. Step scenario_event: Consume an actual distinct Scenario roll with the quest 8–10 threshold; reset only this event report. Step scenario_trigger: The Scenario die is triggered on a result of 8–10. Step ordinary_scenario: A non-triggering actual die event does not retain a prior triggered report. Step objective: Heroes enter on the short side. The statue stands at the far end, with enemies between it and the heroes. Roll twice on the Encounter Table and place enemies randomly. Step encounter_handoff: Request the actual two source encounters and random placement once; no actor/statistic/coordinate invented. Step unresolved_attempt_scope: The source does not say whether once per turn belongs to party or hero; unresolved context cannot authorize an attempt. Step new_turn: A distinct actual owned turn makes this source opportunity available; never reset merely on phase change. Step refit_attempt: Once all enemies are dead, a hero standing in front of the statue can try to refit the stone once per turn by making a DEX test. Step request_dex: Request the actual pending DEX result once; a request cannot refit the stone or raise Threat. Step refit_success: A successful DEX test puts the stone in place. Step refit_failure: A failed attempt increases Threat by 1. Step failure_threat: Apply printed +1 once within uncontested below-maximum scope; request at maximum is separately unresolved. Step maximum_threat: At printed maximum 20, preserve raw +1 and request actual boundary accounting once; do not guess a cap or exceed maximum. Step curse_ends: Actual stone return ends only this owned nullification; numeric Luck Points are preserved. Step reward: Once the stone is in place the heroes head home. Once home, the nobleman pays 300 c per hero.
- `procedure.sanctum_prayer`: The Inner Sanctum prints no fee or duration for praying. Whether the temple fee of 50 c and the one day from Pray at the Local Temples also apply is issue.guild.sanctum_prayer_fee; the caller supplies the reading in sanctum_fee_reading, and without it no prayer is made.
- `procedure.sanctum_prayer`: Each hero may choose only one temple before each quest. Whether a hero who has prayed may pray again to the same god before the next quest is not stated (issue.guild.same_god_prayer_retry).
- `procedure.sanity_loss`: Certain room events: See Exploration Card. Supply the actual card loss amount; no absent card effect is invented.
- `procedure.scenario_die`: The Start of Turn sequence chart (PDF 90) shows the same branch: Roll Scenario die (1d10), 1-8 to Move heroes, 9-10 to Roll Threat (1d20).
- `procedure.scenario_die`: The not-in-battle Threat table result 20 (Add +1 on all Scenario die roll for the remainder of the dungeon. This can only happen once.) is carried by threat_trigger: a +1 on a d10 roll reaches 9 from a roll of 8, so the caller supplies a trigger one lower.
- `procedure.settlement_activities_and_overnight`: Structural reading, not printed text: each call handles one hero for one phase. A hero spends at most one Activity Point per day, so an activity costing N occupies days start to start + N - 1 and the party stays at the inn through that night. Departure needs a day after the last activity and the last occupied day. Create a Scroll and Enchant Objects counters run between quests: they reset when the hero leaves on a quest, not on arrival, and one object excludes scroll attempts and the reverse.
- `procedure.settlement_activities_and_overnight`: Recovery modelling, not printed text: a 2d6 (inn or own home) or 1d6 (stable) HP roll that would take a hero above the recorded maximum is not applied and returns issue.phase4.recovery_bounds; it does not block the Mana, Energy and Luck restoration. The printed "only half (RDD) of each stat" settles rounding (round down) but not whether half means half of the maximum, of the missing amount or of the current value, so the stable steps apply only caller-supplied half-stat amounts (stable_outcome_supplied) that stay within each maximum, and otherwise return issue.phase4.recovery_bounds; the stable recovery applies at most once per hero and night and keeps the mandatory morning departure. Staying at the house skips only the inn charge; recovery there follows the inn branch.
- `procedure.settlement_arrival`: Structural reading, not printed text: the event threshold, the rolls and the Quest Book results are supplied. Visit counters belong to one genuine arrival, so a repeated call in the same visit neither rerolls the event nor reopens the offer; a second quests call and a roll offering no quest return issue.settlement.quest_availability_repeat. Rejecting every offered quest forces departure under the printed "If none of the quests are interesting to the party, they must move to another settlement". The 2-quest limit applies to every settlement except Silver City and the five named in issue.settlement.quest_offer_scope (Durburim, Birnheim, The Outpost, Freyfell, Whiteport). Map geometry is supplied.
- `procedure.slaying_fiend`: Structural reading, not printed text: Preserve Random location, eight corridors/eight rooms, Beast encounters, printed Special Rules dash and Reward None. At actual objective entry, persist one d6 prior-wound branch and subtract its actual result from initial 45 HP before the fight. Resolve hero d3 distance from the short-side door and Molgor d6 distance from the idol toward heroes once. Both preparations precede battle readiness. Actual fiend-down outcome unlocks a gold pile and two unlocked/untrapped objective chests; request their Treasure Table outcomes once without inventing gold amount or collecting contents. Current battle HP, external abilities, chest content/collection and generic quest completion/abandonment remain separately owned. Source initial Threat d4+2, same-as-start minimum and maximum 20 are initialized once from an actual result; battle readiness also requires that source setup. Step request_threat: Request actual initial d4 once; source start/minimum cannot be inferred from current Threat. Step initial_threat: Initialize source Threat once as actual d4+2, minimum equal to that start and maximum 20. Replay cannot lower/replace current Threat. Step setup: Initialize the printed quest layout/equipment distinctions once; unavailable ability mechanics and random site remain separate. Step snapshot_selection: Persist the actual initial d6 choice before delayed secondary dice resolution. Step request_wounds: Request actual wound selection/result once; do not substitute another branch or invent wounds. Step restore_selection: Use the persisted choice, not a changed replay selection, for the once-only HP initialization. Step resolve_actual_wounds: Copy the actual supplied selected wound result into owned working state. Never overwrite the supplied result itself; invalid selected-branch context remains uninitialized. Step fixed_wound: Printed selection 6 is fixed 1, not another die roll. Resolve that known result when no amount is supplied; a conflicting supplied amount remains subject to the invalid-branch disposition. Step wounds_1: Apply only the actual selected wound branch within its printed dice bounds once, before battle. Step wounds_2: Apply only the actual selected wound branch within its printed dice bounds once, before battle. Step wounds_3: Apply only the actual selected wound branch within its printed dice bounds once, before battle. Step wounds_4: Apply only the actual selected wound branch within its printed dice bounds once, before battle. Step wounds_5: Apply only the actual selected wound branch within its printed dice bounds once, before battle. Step wounds_6: Apply only the actual selected wound branch within its printed dice bounds once, before battle. Step invalid_wounds: A supplied amount outside the selected dice branch remains unresolved; it cannot initialize HP or mark battle ready. Step request_placement: Request actual d3/d6 placement once; no geometric square or die result invented. Step placement: Resolve actual supplied hero/Molgor placement once without replay movement. Step ready: Both source preparations must be complete before this checkpoint reports battle readiness. This does not execute battle. Step aftermath: Actual fiend-down outcome unlocks the printed gold find and two unlocked/untrapped objective chests once. No advertised payment or gold amount is invented. Step treasure_handoff: Hand off the two unlocked, untrapped objective-chest treasure outcomes once; request alone does not collect contents or credit the unspecified gold.
- `procedure.threat_roll`: The Start of Turn sequence chart (PDF 90) draws the same branches: Roll Threat (1d20); ≤Threat to Roll on Threat Table (next page) and Execute result; >Threat to 20? (yes! Lower Threat -5, no! Raise Threat +1); every branch then reaches Move heroes. A natural 20 takes the -5 and not the +1.
- `procedure.threat_roll`: The Threat decrease is supplied from the rolled table row, and the floor of 2 or the quest minimum is core.threat.floor; the +1 for a roll above the level is also core.threat.increase.threat_roll_exceeded.
- `procedure.threat_roll`: Executing the rolled table result (Wandering Monster, extra Exploration Card, encounter risk, trap, Scenario die bonus, or the in-battle boons) is the invoked table row, not this procedure.
- `procedure.trap_resolution`: The trap card (its modifiers next to the eye and the cogs, affected actors, damage and any saving throw) is not in this book; those values are supplied inputs or unresolved.
- `procedure.trap_resolution`: Detected Mimic disarming or deliberate triggering is not defined by these paragraphs; it is resolved from its card, without assuming it behaves as an ordinary device.
- `procedure.trap_resolution`: Disarming follows the designer ruling (changelog 2.21 entry 121): a lock pick or a trap disarming kit is needed. The printed No Lock Picks are needed stays quoted.
- `procedure.travel_event_check`: Every hex below the white dotted line is in the Ancient Land and is a Desert Hex (PDF 126, chapter introduction), so Ancient Lands travel uses the desert threshold and the Desert Event Cards.
- `procedure.travel_food_and_rest`: Changelog 2.21 entry 166 changes the printed "Party Morale is also lowered by 4" into "Party Morale is also lowered by 1 per character (Mercenaries included, not dogs)". The printed sentence stays quoted; step hunger_morale applies the ruling, keeping the printed duration ("This lasts until they eat again") and the printed non-cumulation across days. This is the same hunger penalty as the "A character is hungry" row of the Party Morale table (character.morale.event.hungry, changelog 2.21 entry 148), applied once, not a second one; step hunger_morale applies it itself, and the rule is listed as the dependency hungry_morale for reference only, never invoked as a handoff, so a consumer does not subtract it twice.
- `procedure.travel_food_and_rest`: Changelog 2.21 entries 76 and 167 change "each hero" into "the party" ("When travelling in the Ancient Lands, the party requires 2 rations per day"); step ancient_food_requirement applies it. A supply of exactly 1 ration in the Ancient Lands stays issue.travel.partial_rations.
- `procedure.travel_food_and_rest`: The food phase resolves the party's rations or Foraging once per day; the hero phase applies that shared result to one character's Constitution; the rest phase recovers one hero. Rest in a settlement is not this rest ("If the party decides to end their movement in a settlement or the City Hex, they have to pay to stay at the inn overnight. Go to the chapter on 'Settlements' for more information.").
- `procedure.travel_skirmish_setup`: The page says "four kinds of outdoor tiles" and prints four run-in headings (Roads; Wilderness; Village, Camp, Standing Stones, Quest site entrance, City street; Desert). The tiles, the Event Cards and the mini-quests are physical components; their setup instructions, enemy statistics and map geometry are supplied.
- `procedure.wandering_monster`: Iron Wedges (Appendix III) says any enemy needs 6 AP to pass a wedged door; this heading says a 5-6 roll lets the token continue. Both are preserved: issue.phase6.iron_wedges_movement.
- `procedure.wandering_monster`: Movement geometry, the exact route and the distance to the heroes are supplied spatial facts.
- `procedure.wandering_monster`: The page does not say whether the 2-6 (or 5-6) roll at a closed door is the turn's 1d6 direction roll or a separate roll; door_roll is supplied: issue.wandering.door_roll.

- `recipe.cure_poison`: Result name retained without equating to differently named preparation.

- `state_machine.battle`: Structural reading, not printed text: the battle lifecycle spans three chapters. Initiative rules say when the lifecycle starts and how activation order is drawn; the turn rules say what happens to the interrupted turn; the combat chapter says when the battle ends. State assignments follow the source; no transition is invented.
- `state_machine.battle`: Battle-end other than all enemies dead (fleeing enemies, quest-fought endpoints) is not sourced in the extracted pages; only the all-enemies-dead condition is modelled.
- `state_machine.quest_dungeon`: Structural reading, not printed text: this is the lifecycle of one dungeon quest occurrence from the settlement offer to leaving the dungeon. The offered, rejected, accepted and departed states follow Taking on Quests, Rejecting a Quest, Available quests and Leaving on a Quest (PDF 132–133); acceptance and departure are recorded by procedure.quest_acceptance and procedure.quest_departure. Abandonment retains the layout; returning resumes the same task after repopulation and fresh checks. Actual task achievement permits leaving without retracing. This machine does not execute rewards, infer source-specific task completion or reset for a repeated quest; a legitimately repeated quest has a separate instance.
